newsitem.title: USA: Dow gyrates to record as IBM shares jump.
newsitem.headline: Dow gyrates to record as IBM shares jump.

text.p: The Dow Jones industrial average climbed to its eighth straight record high Friday as Dow component IBM raced to its best finish since before the 1987 stock market crash.

"IBM is a bellwether for the market which has been roaring along. But just because it's trading at levels near before the '87 crash doesn't mean we're going into a tailspin anytime soon," said Philip Orlando, chief investment officer at Value Line Asset Management.
The 30-share Dow industrials surged 35.03 points to 6,348.03. It climbed 128.21 points for the week after last week's 198-point jump.
Meanwhile, International Business Machines Corp. jumped 8-1/8 to 145, giving the Dow the equivalent of a 25-point boost. IBM shares last ended above 140 on Oct. 15, 1987.
IBM's rally was aided by Merrill Lynch analyst Daniel Mandresh who raised his 12-month IBM price target to $195 from $155. The analyst cited the computer giant's fourth-quarter outlook.
"Mandresh is considered to be 'Mr. IBM,' so when he talks, investors listen," Orlando said.
The 30-share Dow bounced between virtually unchanged and a gain of 65 points Friday, and was spurred by the expiration of November stock index options and equity options.
In the broader market, advancing issues led declines 1,242 to 1,177 on very heavy volume of 526 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange, swollen by the options expirations.

The string of eight highs for the Dow sent Wall Street historians poring over the record books for a longer stretch but no answers had been found by late Friday. A few guessed a longer run may have occurred in the months before the October 1987 crash.

As for the overall market, Abby Joseph Cohen, co-chair of Goldman Sachs' investment policy committee, said the outlook for stocks remains "constructive. The fundamental support for the market is good. We think prices can go higher since we're in the midst of a long-lasting period of growth."
"It may not be as vigorous as we've seen but it's rapid enough," Cohen added. She noted that inflation remains under control and the recent bond rally is helping stocks.

The Nasdaq Composite fell from record levels, down 8.56 to 1,261.80, and was up 4.3 for the week. Weakness in chip maker Intel Corp., which lost four to 115-7/8, hurt the technology-laden Nasdaq index.
Like many other analysts, William LeFevre, a senior market analyst at Ehrenkrantz King Nussbaum, was surprised by the length and strength of the Dow's latest streak.
"I'm surprised it continues unchecked for this long. We've only had one down Dow day this month" on Nov. 1, he said.

"Does this run mean that Wall Street likes the re-election of (President Bill) Clinton? No. It means we're relieved you have one party in the White House and another in Congress and one will act as a restraint to the other. There'll be no excessive liberal or conservative moves....Corporate America is not obstructed and that's the way they look at it."
Among individual issues, Vimpel-Communications, the Russian wireless telecommunications company, jumped 8-1/2 to 29 in its Wall Street debut.
Dow component Texaco added 2-3/4 to 101-1/8. The company said after the close that it settled a racial discrimination lawsuit that had led to calls for a boycott of Texaco stations.
Health Management tumbled 7-5/8 to 14-1/2 after the company issued a profit warning, the latest in a string from health information services companies.

ITI Technologies lost 18-3/16 points to 11-15/16 after news its single largest customer, ADT Security Systems, said it will reduce purchase orders during the first quarter of 1997. Dain Bosworth cut ITI to hold from buy.
The Standard & Poor's composite index of 500 stocks rose 1.74 points to 737.62, its second straight record. The index added 6.79 on the week.
The NYSE Composite rose 1.01 to 390.02, also a record, and was up 3.7 from last Friday. The average share rose 11 cents.
The American Stock Exchange index rose 0.05 to 585.41, and added 5.02 on the week.
The Wilshire Associates Equity Index -- the market value of NYSE, American and Nasdaq issues -- was at a new high of 7,128.176, up 6.982 or 0.10 percent. The index rose 58.289 from a week ago.
